note: First election of Portadown Borough Council. The Governor (Earl Granville) granted the Urban Council's petition for a charter of incorporation, announced in the Belfast Gazette of 18 July 1947 (Belfast News-Letter, 19 July 1947, p. 5); the borough council of three aldermen and twelve councillors held its first meeting on 2 October 1947, when R. J. Magowan was elected first Mayor (Belfast News-Letter, 3 October 1947, p. 3). Geo. McGowan, returning officer, received the nominations on Friday 5 September 1947: twelve for the twelve councillorships, and four for the three aldermanships. Aldermen were elected by the whole borough, polled Thursday 25 September 1947 and declared on the 26th; 68 per cent poll. Cassells, Johnston and Finlay were retiring councillors standing as Unionist Association candidates; William Wright, a newcomer, son and grandson of former councillors, stood as an Independent and headed the poll.
